---
title: "Ecology"
---

Ecology explains how living systems are organised and how energy, matter, and
information move through them. Evolution explains how populations change across
generations. Together they provide a framework for understanding biodiversity,
adaptation, and environmental change.

## A step-by-step route

Work through these topics in order. Each page introduces a reusable idea and
points toward the next scale of biological organisation.

1. [Ecological foundations](ecological-foundations.qmd) — levels of organisation, scale, niches, and feedback.
2. [Evidence and ecological study](evidence-ecological-study.qmd) — observation, experiments, sampling, and uncertainty.
3. [Environment and limiting factors](environment-limiting-factors.qmd) — abiotic conditions, resources, tolerance, and climate.
4. [Species distributions](species-distributions.qmd) — range, dispersal, occupancy, and metapopulations.
5. [Evolution and natural selection](evolution-natural-selection.qmd) — variation, inheritance, fitness, and adaptation.
6. [Heredity and phylogeny](heredity-phylogeny.qmd) — genes, traits, common ancestry, and reading trees.
7. [Speciation and macroevolution](speciation-macroevolution.qmd) — reproductive isolation, divergence, and extinction.
8. [Population ecology](population-ecology.qmd) — growth, regulation, demography, and life histories.
9. [Community ecology](community-ecology.qmd) — species interactions, competition, predation, and succession.
10. [Ecosystems and biodiversity](ecosystems-biodiversity.qmd) — energy flow, biogeochemical cycles, food webs, and conservation.

## Anchor resource

::: {.callout-tip}
### Start here

[Lecture 1: Introduction to Ecology](https://kevintshoemaker.github.io/NRES-470/LECTURE1.html)
is a useful first pass through the central questions and vocabulary of ecology.
Use it alongside the pages above, then return to it when a concept needs a
second explanation.
:::

## How to study this section

For each topic, be able to define the key terms, draw the main diagram from
memory, explain one example, and identify what would change the prediction.
Keep examples at more than one scale: an individual, a population, a community,
and an ecosystem.

## Further resources

- [OpenStax Biology 2e](https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e) — accessible chapters on evolution, ecology, populations, and communities.
- [Nature Education: Scitable](https://www.nature.com/scitable/) — concise biology explanations and references.
- [OpenStax Concepts of Biology](https://openstax.org/details/books/concepts-biology) — a shorter introduction when the full Biology 2e treatment is too detailed.
